summary: Menlo Park's median home value exceeds $2 million, yet it sits on just 17.4 square miles of mostly flat bayside terrain — making it one of the smallest and most expensive municipalities in the San Francisco Peninsula corridor, square foot for square foot. The reason is largely geographic proximity to an extraordinary concentration of employers: Meta's sprawling campus anchors the eastern edge near the Bayfront, and Sand Hill Road — arguably the densest corridor of venture capital firms on Earth — runs along the city's western boundary into the foothills approaching the Santa Cruz Mountains. With a median household income around $207,000, the home-price-to-income ratio still lands near 10:1, meaning even top-quintile earners face serious leverage to buy. Daily highs average a remarkably mild 68°F year-round with over nine hours of sunshine per day, and the flat topography makes cycling practical — the city connects to the Bay Trail network along the marshlands east of US-101, though that freeway does bisect the city into distinct halves, with the downtown core and tree-lined residential streets to the west and more campus-style commercial development to the east. Downtown Santa Cruz Avenue offers a genuine walkable strip of restaurants and independent shops, but the evening pace is quiet-suburban rather than bustling. Menlo Park is less a self-contained town than a very expensive front porch for Silicon Valley's financial and technical infrastructure, where the commute may be short but the cost of entry is not.
